title: Fail-Open Execution without set -euo pipefail
platform_conditions: POSIX sh supports set -e/-u but NOT pipefail; set -o pipefail requires bash, ksh or zsh; 'local x=$(cmd)' masking exit status is a bash/ksh behavior
security_mechanism: Without set -e the shell keeps executing after any failure, so a failed signature or checksum verification (gpg verify, sha256sum -c) prints an error and the next line installs or runs the unverified artifact anyway. In a pipeline the exit status comes from the last command by default, so 'curl ... | sh' succeeds even when the download failed or was tampered mid-stream; pipefail exists to surface this and is POSIX-only in the non-portable direction. Two quiet paths add to it: 'local x=$(cmd)' discards the substitution's exit status because 'local' succeeds, and 'cmd || true' converts any failure — including a failed permission change — into success.

source_sink_clues.source: Installer and CI steps whose inputs are fetched or attacker-influenced (downloaded packages, PR-modified manifests), where a silent failure advances to the next stage instead of aborting.
source_sink_clues.sink: Verification-then-act sequences (checksum/signature check followed by install, chmod/chown, service start) in scripts lacking set -euo pipefail at the top, or where '|| true', unguarded cd, or 'local x=$(cmd)' neutralizes a failure on the security-relevant step

tracking_guards: Check set -euo pipefail is set before any security-relevant command (with set -o pipefail verified as supported by the interpreter); check verification commands are chained explicitly (verify && install, or if ! verify; then exit 1; fi); check cd is followed by an exit-status test or set -e is active; check no '|| true' on permission, signature, or checksum steps; check 'local' is split from its assignment when the exit status matters.
not_candidate_when: set -euo pipefail is active and verification commands run directly (no pipeline or || true softening), each security step's status is checked explicitly with if/&&, or the script's only consumers are non-security steps whose failure mode is a build error rather than a privilege or integrity change.
public_references: CWE-754: Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/754.html
